note: Hypotonia and behavioral disturbances consistently co-occur at high frequencies in FBXO11 cohorts, distinguishing it from isolated neurobehavioral phenotypes.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 21 individuals with FBXO11 variants, hypotonia and behavioural dysregulation were among the most prevalent findings, each occurring in 62% of patients.

source.title: Defining FBXO11-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder: Clinical, Molecular and Facial Assessment of 21 Patients
source.quote: Mild intellectual disability (86%), facial dysmorphism (67%), hypotonia (62%), and behavioural dysregulation (62%) were the most prevalent features.

evidence.text: In a Chinese cohort of 12 individuals with FBXO11 variants, hypotonia was observed in only 1 patient, indicating variability across distinct populations or variant types.

source.title: FBXO11 variants are associated with intellectual disability and variable clinical manifestation in Chinese affected individuals
source.quote: hypotonia (1/12), and auditory hallucinations and hallucinations (1/12).
